target.title: fix(openclaw): prevent private state races during publication
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where OpenClaw bridge state publication or recursive cleanup could be redirected, blocked indefinitely, or race with another process when private path ancestry or mutation claims changed concurrently.

## Why This Change Was Made

Private publication ancestry is now created with owner-only permissions, mutations use identity-checked process claims, existing parents and claims are validated by POSIX ownership or Windows ACLs, stale claims recover without unbounded path growth, and cleanup preserves files whose identity changed under it. The boundary remains limited to Crabline OpenClaw private-file handling.

## User Impact

Operators can rely on private bridge state publication and cleanup to fail closed under path substitution, concurrent mutation, stale owners, and ownership or ACL drift instead of mutating an untrusted path.

## Evidence

- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm exec vitest run test/openclaw-private-file.test.ts` (`80 passed`, `4 skipped` on macOS)
- `pnpm lint`
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- Codex autoreview with `gpt-5.6-sol` / high reasoning: clean after the final directory-compaction race fix
- Native Windows Crabbox focused suite: pending
- Linux Crabbox `pnpm verify`: pending
- Public-data scrub: no private paths, hostnames, addresses, or contact data found
- Changelog entry included
